question: Can one motion decoder with separate free codes reconstruct moving and static futures from the same initial GS, without destroying the original motion?
examples_per_update: one moving and one static target for the same initial condition and horizon
initial_motion_codes: Original free codes paired with the two-window warm decoder
initial_static_codes: Optimized 540-step static codes from the fixed-decoder diagnostic
moving_supervision: Actual future state and source RGB, with existing full/ROI/motion-weighted loss and 0.1 latent loss
static_supervision: Repeated S0 state and same-camera codec-rendered S0; full/ROI/motion-weighted loss and 0.1 latent loss. Motion weight is the same-camera difference between paired moving codec reference and static codec reference and is used only in offline loss/evaluation.
condition: Motion and static branches share identical S0 condition and target camera; their only decoder input difference is continuous code. True future is never supplied to decoder condition.
predeclared_exploratory_gate: Anchor moving MAE <= 1.10 times original warm decoder, at least 16/18 static predictions closer to their static reference than their moving reference, and mean static error <= half mean reference difference. All are necessary but not sufficient; visual review of object retention, pose and absence of black artifacts is mandatory.
limits: Two known windows in one training video, one initialization and fixed short budget. Offline free-code capacity diagnostic, not a trained Q-Former, full-168 teacher, AR, cross-video generalization or proof of impossibility.
